hints: Notice the vertical axis is displacement to the right, so positive means shifted right and negative means shifted left from equilibrium.
Compare the sign of displacement just to the left and just to the right of the zero crossings B and D.
A compression needs particles on the left pushed right and particles on the right pushed left, so both sides move toward the same point.
walkthrough: Identify what the graph shows: at one instant, $displacement$ to the right is plotted against $distance$ along the wave travelling left to right.
Recall that a compression is where air particles are pushed closest together, so particles on the left must have moved right ($positive$) and particles on the right must have moved left ($negative$).
At B the curve crosses zero with falling slope: just left of B displacement is positive and just right of B displacement is negative.
That means material from both sides has moved toward B, increasing the local density, which is the definition of the centre of a compression.
At D the opposite happens: just left displacement is negative and just right displacement is positive, so material has moved away from D, forming a rarefaction.
Points A and C are maximum right and maximum left displacements where the slope is zero, so neighbours move almost together with no crowding. This is option B.

options.A: At A displacement to the right is maximum, so neighbouring particles are displaced by almost the same amount and are not crowded together.
options.B: Particles just left of B are displaced to the right and particles just right of B are displaced to the left, so they move together to form a compression.
options.C: At C displacement to the left is maximum, so neighbouring particles are displaced by almost the same amount and are not crowded together.
options.D: Particles just left of D are displaced to the left and particles just right of D are displaced to the right, so they spread apart to form a rarefaction.
